text: The meadow is an elevated grassy mountain slope and plateau biome filled with patches of flowers, turquoise-green grass and tall grass, where sheep, donkeys, and rabbits spawn.
search_text: Meadow > Overview: The meadow is an elevated grassy mountain slope and plateau biome filled with patches of flowers, turquoise-green grass and tall grass, where sheep, donkeys, and rabbits spawn.

text:
Meadows generate elevated in cool to temperate inland regions. They take several forms, including thin strips on mountain slopes, massive standalone plateaus, and valleys inside mountain rings.
Toward higher elevations, snowy slopes or groves often generate between a meadow and high peaks, though meadows can also border jagged peaks or frozen peaks directly. As terrain lowers, plains, taigas, forests, birch forests, or flower forests tend to surround meadows. Cherry groves can also border meadows, especially where humidity is low, while pale gardens often do so where humidity is high.
Although any cave biome may generate underground, dripstone caves and the deep dark are by far the most common.

text:
The meadow is a high altitude counterpart to the plains biome. It is covered by most flowers controlled by a gradient, meaning that it can continue for hundreds of blocks with the same type of flower. In addition to this, the ground is covered by lots of short grass and wildflowers, along with some tall grass.
Rarely, a lone oak or birch tree of any size can generate and always has a bee nest. Both pillager outposts and plains villages can generate in this biome, making this the only mountain biome where villages can generate. , unlike most Overworld biomes, sugar canes and pumpkin patches cannot generate here. Abandoned camps sometimes generate in meadows.
Just like other mountain biomes, emerald ores can be found in meadows, especially at higher altitudes, and both coal and iron ores are commonly found here. Infested block blobs also naturally generate in meadows.
, meadows are cold and allow snowfall above Y=200±8, however, this never occurs on natural terrain.
The only passive mobs that can spawn here are rabbits, sheep, and occasionally donkeys.

text:
, the base melee attack damage is calculated differently for different entities:
For players, the calculation sequence for base melee attack damage is as follows:
Get the player's base attack value.
Add the main hand item damage.
Calculate the Strength status effect.
Calculate the Weakness status effect.
For example, the base melee attack damage of a player holding a wooden sword with both Strength II and Weakness I effects would be calculated as:
1 (Player base attack value) + 4 (Wooden sword damage) = 5
(5 × 1.3 + 1) × 1.3 + 1 = 10.75 (Strength II)
10.75 × 0.8 - 0.5 = 8.1 (Weakness I)
For most non-player entities, the calculation sequence for base melee attack damage is as follows:
Get the mob's base attack value.
Calculate the Strength status effect.
Calculate the Weakness status effect.
Add the main hand item damage.
For example, the base melee attack damage of a zombie holding a wooden sword with both Strength II and Weakness I effects would be calculated as:
3 (Zombie base attack value)
(3 × 1.3 + 1) × 1.3 + 1 = 7.37 (Strength II)
7.37 × 0.8 - 0.5 = 5.396 (Weakness I)
5.396 + 4 (Wooden sword damage) = 9.396

text:
The attack cooldown is a meter below the crosshair that reduces damage when attacking before the meter is full. An attack cooldown percentage of 84.8% or above is also required for critical hits, sprint-knockback attacks, and sweep attacks to activate. The indicator can be optionally changed to display next to the hotbar instead of under the crosshair in Video Settings.
Attack speed is controlled by the attack_speed attribute. The default value is 4, meaning that 4 full-damage melee attacks can be performed per , however damage immunity allows only 2 of these attacks to connect against a single target. The Haste effect increases attack speed by 10% per level, and the Mining Fatigue effect decreases it by 10% per level. Spear jab attacks specifically have a forced attack cooldown, meaning they cannot attack at all until they reach 100% cooldown charge.

The time from one melee attack, breaking a block, or switching the main-hand item to the next melee attack that can deal full damage is called the attack cooldown time. The ratio of the time elapsed since the above actions to the total attack cooldown time is the attack cooldown completion. The number of full-damage melee attacks a player can perform per is the attack speed.

text:
Attack cooldown time can be calculated from attack speed. If the attack speed is s , the attack cooldown time T is \frac{20}{s} game ticks. Since game ticks do not have decimal values, the actual attack cooldown time is rounded: if the decimal part is greater than 0.5, it is rounded up; otherwise, it is rounded down.
Attack cooldown completion can also be calculated from these values. If the time since the last melee attack, block break, or main-hand item switch is t game ticks, then the attack cooldown completion p is \text{clamp}(\frac{t+0.5}{T}, 0, 1) . The visual component related to attack cooldown completion is the attack indicator, which has a slight difference in rendering percentage compared to the actual attack cooldown completion: \text{clamp}(\frac{t}{T}, 0, 1) , meaning the displayed value lags by half a game tick.
Attack cooldown affects base melee attack damage, enchanted attack damage, and additional attack damage differently. Given attack cooldown completion p , the base melee attack damage is modified by 0.2+0.8p^2 , the enchanted attack damage by p , while additional attack damage remains unaffected. The effect on base melee attack damage can stack with critical hits.

text:
For most entities, the attack range is defined as a horizontally extended area beyond their collision box, referred to below as the attack bounding box. Similarly, the attacked entity has a range within which it can be struck, referred to as the hit bounding box. A melee attack can occur when the attack bounding box intersects with the hit bounding box. Entities performing melee attacks must also maintain a clear line of sight to the attacked entity, preventing attacks through blocks. Since entities cannot see themselves, they cannot perform melee attacks on themselves. As of Mounts of Mayhem, there is a second minimum bounding box representing the minimum reach of the entity, which will prevent the attacker from attacking the attacked entity if it is within its range.
The attack bounding boxes for an entity are obtained for the entity's minimum range (if non-zero) and maximum range boxes as follows:
Get the entity's collision box. If the entity is riding another entity, use the collision bounding box of both entities, with the height range taken from the entity's collision box.
Expand the collision box by the reach for this box (either minimum or maximum).
If the entity is a ravager, reduce the attack bounding box by 0.05 blocks horizontally.
The hit bounding box is calculated as follows:
If the entity is not riding another entity, the hit bounding box is the entity's collision box.

text:
When melee attack damage is dealt, the attacked entity will be pushed backward; this is knockback. The horizontal direction of knockback aligns with the attacker's viewpoint. The knockback of an attack is dependent on the player's weapon, and is controlled by the attack knockback attribute.
The magnitude of knockback depends on whether the attacker is sprinting and the item in their main hand. This is described using knockback strength. Knockback strength is 0 by default. If the main-hand item has the knockback enchantment, the knockback strength increases by the enchantment's level.

text: , only players can knock back non-living entities. Knockback strength determines the knockback speed, which is half of the knockback strength. If the target of the knockback is a non-living entity, it receives a vertical motion of 0.1 blocks per tick (2 blocks per second) and a horizontal knockback speed. If the target is a living entity, the knockback speed is reduced based on its knockback resistance (attribute knockback_resistance ). If the knockback resistance is 1, knockback does not occur. Next, the entity's horizontal movement speed is halved, and knockback speed is applied. If the entity is touching the ground, its vertical speed is also halved, and upward knockback speed is applied. However, the final vertical speed does not exceed 0.4 blocks per tick (8 blocks per second). After knockback occurs, the attacking entity immediately stops sprinting, and their horizontal speed is reduced to 60% of its original value.

text:
All weapons aside from spears have the ability to do critical hits, which deal 50% extra damage.
To perform a critical hit, the following conditions must be met:
The player must be falling.
The player's attack cooldown percentage must be at 84.8% or above.
The player must not be sprinting, as this causes a sprint-knockback attack to be performed instead.
In , players ordinarily cannot perform critical hits while sprinting, because a sprint-knockback attack is performed instead. However, by continuing to hold down the sprint key after performing a sprint-knockback attack, all successive hits can be critical hits, and sprint-knockback attacks become impossible until the sprint is ended.
In , critical hits can be performed simultaneously with sprint-knockback attacks.
The player must not be on the ground, meaning they must not be standing on any surface with block collision boxes.
The player must not be inside climbable blocks (like ladders, vines, cobwebs, or trapdoors that are open on the same side as a ladder).
The player must not be in water (they can be in lava, however).
The player must not be riding on a mount or riding in a vehicle.
The player must not have Slow Falling, Blindness, or Levitation effects.

text:
All weapons aside from spears have the ability to do sprint-knockback attacks, which deal extra knockback while sprinting and cancel the sprint. , sprint-knockback attacks play a unique sound when performed, and they require an attack cooldown charge of at least 84.8%.
In , sprint-knockback attacks cannot be performed at the same time as critical hits or sweep attacks. If a sprint-knockback attack is performed at the same time as a critical hit, the sprint-knockback attack takes priority. They can however be performed at the same time as smash attacks and crushing blows.
The extra inflicted knockback stacks with the Knockback enchantment. Like the Knockback enchantment, sprint-knockback attacks do not increase knockback against entities that are immune to knockback, such as iron golems or shielding players. The only exceptions to this are armor stands and boats, which ordinarily do not take knockback when hit but do when hit by a sprint-knockback attack.

text:
Swords have the special ability to do sweep attacks, which deal to nearby entities with a gale particle.
A sweep attack occurs only if all of the following conditions are met:
The attack cooldown percentage is at 84.8% or above.
The player is not performing a critical hit.
The player is not performing a sprint-knockback attack.
The player is on the ground, meaning they must be standing on any solid surface.
The player's mainhand weapon is a sword.
The melee attack is able to do damage.
The difference in movement distance between the current game tick and the previous tick does not exceed the movement_speed attribute value (default: 0.1 blocks per tick, or 2 blocks per second).
The player's mainhand weapon has Sweeping Edge.
The range of a sweep attack is determined by both the attacked entity and the player's position. Based on the attacked entity's collision box, the range extends 1 block horizontally in all directions and 0.25 blocks vertically both up and down. All entities within 3 blocks of the player (excluding the attacking player themselves, the primary attacked entity, and armor stands with the tag set to true ) will be affected by the sweep attack. Similar to melee attacks, sweep attacks also apply knockback. However, knockback from sweep attacks is not affected by the knockback enchantment or sprinting. If the affected entity has 0 knockback resistance, the sweep attack applies a knockback speed of 0.4 blocks per tick.

text:
Axes have the special ability to do crushing blows , which disable the use of the target's shield for 5 seconds . Crushing blows are triggered only against targets that are actively holding their shield up.
Crushing blows affect all of the target's shields, rather than affecting only the one that was being used. Crushing blows do not trigger against targets whose shields are not yet past their 250ms activation delay. Crushing blows are triggered regardless of attack cooldown percentage and, unlike sweep attacks, they can be triggered at the same time as critical hits and sprint-knockback attacks.
Crushing blows work by inflicting a 5 second use cooldown. When a shield is stunned, it cannot be used by pressing the button or . Performing a crushing blow does not consume durability from the axe, in the same way that other attacks do not consume durability when they're blocked by a shield.
, a player whose shield is stunned by a crushing blow becomes immune to knockback for several ticks.
Mobs that wield axes, such as vindicators or piglin brutes, perform crushing blows should they hit a player's shield. The melee attack of a warden also performs a crushing blow should it connect against a player's shield.
In the Java Edition Combat Tests, the stun duration from crushing blows is lengthened by the Cleaving enchantment, at an additional 0.5 seconds per level with a maximum level of III.

text:
Maces have the special ability to do smash attacks, which cause extra damage depending on how many blocks were fallen prior to attacking. Connecting a smash attack clears all fall damage that was accumulated prior to the attack. All entities within 2.5 blocks of the smash attack are knocked back. Like crushing blows, smash attacks are triggered regardless of attack cooldown percentage, and can be triggered at the same time as critical hits and sprint-knockback attacks. Smash attacks trigger the Wind Burst enchantment.
To perform a smash attack, the player must not be grounded or in elytra flight, and the fall height used in calculation is simply the starting height (Y coordinate) minus the ending height (Y coordinate). Descending with an elytra counts as blocks fallen for smash attacks. In , the elytra must be unequipped before attacking for the smash attack to activate, as being in elytra flight does not activate a smash attack. In , unequipping the elytra before attacking is not necessary, as smash attacks activate even while the user is in elytra flight.
A successful smash attack causes a mace to deal extra damage for each of the first 3 blocks fallen, extra damage for each of the next 5 blocks fallen, and extra damage for each block fallen after that. The damage of smash attacks is increased by the Density enchantment by an additional for each block fallen per level of enchantment, at a maximum level of V.

text:
Spears have the special ability to do charge attacks by holding the button, which deal extra damage if the user and the target are moving towards each other fast enough. They must be moving towards each other at ≥4.6 blocks per second to deal damage, and ≥5.1 blocks per second to deal knockback. The damage dealt depends on the velocity of the user and the target. Like jab attacks, charge attacks have a 4.5 block attack reach, 0.125 hitbox inflation, and the 2 block minimum reach requirement, but do not have any sort of cooldown. Charge attacks can hit multiple entities, but only once for each entity.
Charge attacks can still deal damage while the user is standing still, if the target is moving towards the user. The damage done by the charge attack is its damage multiplier multiplied by the velocity of the attacker relative to the target in blocks per second. Charge attacks go through three stages when held out, and the tier of the spear influences the behavior of its charge attacks:
Engaged
The first state of a charge attack, indicated by the spear being held out steadily.
The attack deals damage, inflicts knockback, and dismounts attacked targets from their mounts.
Tired
The second state of a charge attack, indicated by the spear rotating sideways and shaking.
The attack deals damage and inflicts knockback.
Disengaged
The final state of a charge attack, indicated by the spear being lowered down to the bottom of the screen.
The attack only deals damage.

Like jab attacks, charge attacks have a 4.5 block attack reach, 0.125 hitbox inflation, and the 2 block minimum reach requirement, but do not have any sort of cooldown. Charge attacks can hit multiple entities, but only once for each entity.
Charge attacks can still deal damage while the user is standing still, if the target is moving towards the user. The damage done by the charge attack is its damage multiplier multiplied by the velocity of the attacker relative to the target in blocks per second. Charge attacks go through three stages when held out, and the tier of the spear influences the behavior of its charge attacks:
Engaged
The first state of a charge attack, indicated by the spear being held out steadily.
The attack deals damage, inflicts knockback, and dismounts attacked targets from their mounts.
Tired
The second state of a charge attack, indicated by the spear rotating sideways and shaking.
The attack deals damage and inflicts knockback.
Disengaged
The final state of a charge attack, indicated by the spear being lowered down to the bottom of the screen.
The attack only deals damage.

text:
Melee attacks apply mob's base melee attack damage and deal damage to the target entity in mob_attack damage type. Most mobs perform one melee attack per second, targeting a single intended target for the melee attack, without accidentally harming other targets.
Some mobs melee attack in a different way and have special effects:
Players can perform a melee attack on a mob or another player by clicking the button while holding any item to deal damage. Players have a greater melee attack range than most mobs and an unlimited attack frequency, allowing them to continuously attack targets without being reached by most mobs.
When a player uses a trident enchanted with Riptide collides with an entity, they will automatically perform a melee attack on the entities they collide with.
Cave spiders, husks, wither skeletons, and bees deal status effects to the entities they attack during a melee attack.
Iron golems, as well as hoglins and zoglins in knock their targets into the air during melee attacks.
Polar bears stand on their hind legs and swing their front paws to perform melee attacks.
Entities holding an axe, such as vindicators and piglin brutes, as well as wardens, will disable the target's shield during a melee attack for .
When a wither's health falls below 50%, it performs melee attacks in the form of a dash, destroying most blocks it touches during the dash.

text:
When performing a melee attack, the game first calculates the attack damage the attacker can deal, then applies damage to the attacked entity and attempts to disable the shield. After damage is dealt, it calculates knockback, sweep attack , and Fire Aspect, processes the Thorns enchantment's reflected damage, applies Slowness effect by the Bane of Arthropods to arthropods, and may generate critical hit particles. Finally, the player's exhaustion increases by 0.1 per successful melee attack.
Melee attacks can fail, and failed melee attacks do not deal damage.
If an entity's base melee attack damage is and enchanted attack damage is , the melee attack always fails, making no sound and triggering no damage event. This also prevents players from damaging End crystals and armor stands with melee attacks in such cases.
If an entity can deal more than damage but the attacked entity is immune to this damage or is in a dying state, the melee attack fails, producing a special sound different from a successful melee attack.
If an entity's attack damage is not greater than the last damage of the attacked entity's damage immunity, the melee attack fails, producing a distinct sound.
In all other cases, a melee attack is considered successful, even if the damage is completely negated by the target's defense or damage immunity.

text: Melon seeds can be planted, placing a small stem that grows over time. Once the stem reaches maturity, it attempts to generate a melon block in one of the four immediately adjacent blocks; however, this attempt may fail if the chosen adjacent block is not empty or the block beneath is not an appropriate block (dirt, coarse dirt, rooted dirt, grass block, farmland, podzol, mycelium, moss block, pale moss block, mud, or muddy mangrove roots). Melons take 10 to 30 minutes to grow, which is equal to 0.5 to 1.5 times the length of a daylight cycle. Once a stem has produced a melon, that stem does not produce any further melons until the existing melon is harvested. Melon stems connect only to the melons they produce. For example, if stem A generates a melon adjacent to stem B, stem B does not connect and can still produce another melon. Similarly, if a melon is placed adjacent to stem B, stem B would still be able to produce another melon. The same principle applies for pumpkins. Melons require a light level of 9 or higher to grow.

search_text: Mending > Obtaining: Mending is a treasure enchantment; it can be obtained from non-village structure loot, fishing, raid drops , or by trading with a librarian of any level (or if the "Villager Trade Rebalance" experimental datapack is enabled, a master level swamp librarian).

text:
Any items with Mending in the player's main hand, offhand, or armor slots that are not at maximum durability are repaired by experience orbs collected from any source. The rate of repair is two durability per point of experience contained in the orb.
Experience in the orb is deducted by one point for every two durability points repaired.
Experience left in the orb is added to the player's total experience gauge as normal, but prioritizes mending items. Experience won't be added to the gauge if any items with Mending are able to restore durability.
If multiple equipped items have the enchantment and need to be repaired, one is randomly selected for each experience orb collected. No item or location has priority for repair.
Mending does not select items that are already fully repaired. For example, if the player has a fully repaired helmet and a damaged chestplate, leggings, and boots, only the latter 3 are considered in the random chance to be repaired.
Durability doesn't affect which item is chosen at random. For example, a sword that is one durability point away from being fully repaired has an equal chance of being chosen as a pickaxe that is almost broken, even if this means less experience would be used to repair the sword.
Only one of these items is repaired for each experience orb collected. This means that any experience left on the orb is not used to repair other items and is instead added to the player's total experience gauge as normal.

If a Mine Ingredient is obtained in the Hub (through commands or using the rooms behind shimmering doors), it can be obtained by right-clicking the Mine Crafter while holding an ingredient.
The mine crafter interface shows a list of all the ingredients that the player hasn’t unlocked, labeled “Undiscovered,” and every ingredient shows a hint on how to obtain them.
Specific ingredients can be obtained with this command:
{{Cmd|1=/give @s minecraft:mine_ingredient[minecraft:world_modifiers={effects : [ ], include_description:1b}, minecraft:world_effect_unlock={}]}}
where is the identifier of the desired ingredient.

text:
Minecarts can be ridden by on them. Once inside, an external impulse may be needed to make the minecart start moving. The player can slowly move the minecart forward at about 8 blocks per second while riding it, by pressing . If the Minecart Experiments experiment is enabled, the game rule can be used to change the max minecart speed. If a mob walks in front of a moving empty minecart, it is pulled into the cart.
After rolling off of the end of a track, a minecart can be pushed around on open blocks. If a minecart is pushed onto or falls onto tracks, it "snaps" to those tracks. When riding a minecart, if the minecart lands on a rail, the player does not take any fall damage.
Unlike with beds, there is no message in the action bar or in chat for attempting to enter a fully occupied minecart.

text: Players can exit the minecart by while riding it. When a player or mob dismounts a minecart, either by choice, by breaking the minecart, or by passing over a powered activator rail, the minecart tries to find a safe ejection destination for the player one block away. First it checks the eight horizontally adjacent blocks in the following order of priority relative to direction of travel: right, left, rear right, rear left, front right, front left, rear, front. A valid destination has a block underneath with a solid (not necessarily full) top surface and a space with enough headroom and width for the passenger to fit in when standing at the center. The space can even contain liquid or have open trapdoors if the mob is slim enough, and presence of other mobs doesn't matter. If no valid destination exists on same horizontal level, the minecart then checks the blocks one above, then one below. For a player, the minecart also checks for crawlable destinations. If still none, the minecart chooses its own location. Once the minecart picks a destination, it actually ejects the passenger one block up in the air and the passenger settles down on its own. Under a low ceiling this may cause one tick of suffocation damage. The air drop exists to allow passengers to land on carpet or bottom slabs.

text:
Minecarts have a predefined speed limit of exactly 8 blocks per second per axis of travel. A minecart traveling diagonally can, therefore, travel up to 11.314 blocks per second. When a minecart comes to a turn it moves diagonally across that turn.
Powered rails powered by redstone give minecarts a boost of speed. Speed is gradually decreased if there are no powered rails to assist its movement, and an unpowered powered rail slows down a minecart rapidly and can stop minecarts even on slopes. The speed decreases at a faster rate when going uphill, compared to when moving horizontally, but a riding player can still move it uphill at the lowest speed . A minecart does not need powered rails to assist its movement down a hill.
Anything in the way of the minecart brings it to a stop. Once a minecart has left the track, it rapidly decelerates within one or two blocks. When mobs touch a minecart, they affect it in the same way a player would, i.e. mobs that move up against a still cart set it in motion.
If a minecart is moving fast enough, it can skip across one block without a track and reattach to a track on the other side, at significantly reduced energy and speed. A minecart's hitbox can skip turns if the minecart is boosted using enough powered rails.
The speed and momentum of a minecart can differ depending on whether or not it is empty, and in the case where a minecart has a container, the speed can differ depending on the quantity and type of items inside.

text:
Three or more minecarts can be merged by placing multiple minecarts on the same rail or by dropping them on a rail from above. Merged minecarts move as a collective, like a train, and can be useful for long-distance transport because while moving in a straight line, they do not need powered rails to keep their speed.
Pushing merged minecarts might cause them to unmerge.
Merged minecarts do not lose speed while traveling on straight rails.
Corners in the rails might cause merged minecarts to unmerge.
Merged minecarts can travel off-rail at half-speed (4 blocks/second). They can travel diagonally if the last rail is a turned rail.

text:
Minecarts are about the same size as a block (1×1). Because of this, a ladder, door, or trapdoor prevents it from falling down a 1×1 hole. Carts on rails also ignore collision in certain situations. A cart traveling uphill, downhill, or on a curve with a block placed in front of it, goes through the block.
A minecart that reaches the end of a rail up against an opaque solid block bounces back, but if the block is transparent then it stops. The minecart can even bounce against an opaque block from a standstill if the rail underneath is powered. A player or mob riding in a minecart does not collide with or suffocate in any transparent blocks but suffocates inside opaque blocks.
Minecarts are completely unaffected by ice, packed ice, and blue ice ; they can also be destroyed by coming in contact with lava, fire and cactus, causing it to drop itself as an item. The last block can be used to automatically destroy the cart and collect it (with a hopper) at the end of a track.

text:
A cart on an ascending rail performs its horizontal movement at a higher position, with the following effects:
A cart traveling downhill does not collide with a block in front of it, but collides with a block one block higher.
A cart can trigger a pressure plate or tripwire above its bounding box in this process, which can't detect the cart when checking for entities. If deactivated when the cart has not moved away, the pressure plate or tripwire is immediately retriggered.
If updates originating from the pressure plate or tripwire break the rail, the cart appears at the higher position.

text:
Most mobs can be picked up when a minecart collides with them. The following mobs, however, cannot be picked up:
Ender dragons, wardens, and withers in both and ;
Bats and iron golems
Creakings, NPCs, agents, sulfur cubes, and 0.75% of zombified piglins
This is much different from boats, which can be entered only by mobs smaller than the boats; even large mobs like ghasts can enter minecarts. In addition to mobs, minecarts can also pick up boats , and armor stands and cameras .
A mob is picked up when a moving minecart on rails collides with the mob, or if the mob walks into a minecart on rails. Additionally, , a minecart can pick up a mob even if stationary or off-rails. It is easier to pick up a mob when a minecart is turning. For the purposes of picking up mobs, the bounding box of a minecart is extended by 0.2 (approx. ) blocks on each direction on the X and Z axes. This means that a minecart can pick up a mob even if the mob is not intersecting the minecart's hitbox.
, mobs in minecarts (except unnamed endermites) don't despawn, and don't count toward the mob cap.
Mobs cannot control the minecart, unless they are a jockey , and cannot exit the minecart unless the minecart is destroyed or moves onto an active activator rail. , it is also possible to force a mob out of a minecart by reeling it in using a fishing rod.
Tamed pets, as well as endermen, cannot teleport out of minecarts.

text: As minecarts are not mobs, they do not have health. Instead, they have a damage system. For every of damage that would be dealt, instead 10 damage is added. Then, whenever the damage is greater than 0, it gets reduced by 1 each game tick. When the damage is greater than 40, the minecart is destroyed and dropped as an item, meaning that weapons dealing more than damage break a minecart in one attack. Players in Creative mode can always destroy a minecart in one attack, but the minecart does not drop as an item.

text:
Minecarts with chests can be placed by on any type of rail.
Chest minecarts' contents can be accessed by pressing button on them. The interaction makes no sounds and the chest does not show the opening or closing animation, unlike regular chests.
Minecarts with chests also lose momentum based on their load. Fuller minecarts with chests will lose momentum faster than emptier ones. In Java Edition, the formula for the percentage of momentum kept is
0.98 + 0.001 * (15 - container_redstone_signal)
where container_redstone_signal is the signal that would be read by a comparator. If in water, this is further multiplied by 0.95.
Another physical property of chest minecarts is their ability to be stacked. While three chests can fit in an area three blocks tall, up to four chest minecarts can fit in the same area. Like other minecarts, an unlimited number of minecarts with chests can exist in the same block space.
Minecarts with chests are also able to interact with hoppers and droppers. Hoppers can take items out from the minecart chest if they are below the track as the minecart rolls over it or put them in if the minecart rolls under a downward facing hopper. Hoppers can also input items if they are facing into the side of the minecart. Droppers can place items into a chest minecart if it is facing into the block space of the chest minecart when it is activated, placing the dispensed item directly into the chest minecart's inventory.

text:
The minecart with command block combines the functionalities of both minecarts and command blocks. Although the minecart visually contains an impulse command block in Java Edition, it functions more similarly to a repeating command block, executing the command once every four game ticks (unlike a repeating command block that repeats every 1 game tick) when on an active activator rail. When it passes over a detector rail with a comparator connected next to it, it outputs the command block's success count value.
The command is executed at the coordinates of the minecart, which can of course move, allowing for command execution relative to an entity without the command.

text: Similarly to other forms of minecart, minecarts with furnaces can be destroyed by attacking them, and doing so drops them as an item. Despite the appearance of the relevant particles, critical hits are not applied to them.
search_text: Minecart with Furnace > Crafting: Similarly to other forms of minecart, minecarts with furnaces can be destroyed by attacking them, and doing so drops them as an item. Despite the appearance of the relevant particles, critical hits are not applied to them.

text:
Minecarts with furnaces are placed in the same way as other minecarts. They do not have a GUI, unlike a furnace. Also unlike a furnace, furnace minecarts can only be powered with coal and charcoal. Other fuel sources, such as blocks of coal or blaze rods, cannot be used.
Minecarts with furnaces can be powered, done by feeding fuel into the furnace minecart with the button. It cannot be powered by a dispenser. The fuel is consumed immediately and it starts to move in the same direction the player clicked toward. Pressing while not holding coal or charcoal plays the hand animation and is supposed to turn it to that direction, but a bug prevents this from happening. Adding fuel increases the duration by an additional 3600 ticks (equal to 180 seconds or 3 minutes). The upper limit is 32767 ticks, approximately 27 minutes.
When powered, minecarts with furnaces cover 240m per minute (4 m/s, slightly slower than walking speed) or 720m per piece of fuel. They do not accelerate beyond this speed when going downhill or on active powered rails, and as long as they remain powered, they do not slow down when going uphill, on inactive powered rails, or when pushing or pulling other minecarts.
If a powered furnace minecart is derailed and then pushed back onto a rail, it starts moving again in the direction it came from, so they are not easily turned around in this state unless a player is nearby to redirect it with .

text:
When a minecart with furnace bumps into another minecart or multiple minecarts, the other minecarts are pushed forward with great speed. The furnace minecart continues on with its own speed. Because of this speed difference, some of the minecarts may end up inside unloaded chunks on straight tracks.
A player can push an unpowered furnace minecart like any other minecart, but other minecarts cannot push it. So for example, placing a new furnace minecart in front of a speeding minecart is to place an immovable object in its path.

text:
A furnace minecart can be made to pull up to four other minecarts. All minecarts in this train move at the constant speed of the furnace minecart. Trains are formed when a minecart is pushed into the back of a powered furnace minecart or a short-enough train. These shunts are fragile at best and easily come undone, but some methods are stronger than others. For example, pushing a minecart into a furnace minecart and then powering the furnace gives a weaker shunt than pushing the furnace minecart into the other minecart against a wall, and then powering the furnace in the other direction.
Minecarts with furnaces can climb up steep inclines while pushing other minecarts as long as they have fuel. If a minecart with furnace reaches a slope while pulling another minecart, the pulled minecart is switched to the forward position so that it can be pushed along the slope instead of pulled.
A high-speed minecart running into the back of a furnace minecart going in the same direction automatically creates a weak shunt with it, pulling it along.
Pulling a minecart with TNT causes it to explode.
When a train comes to a turn, the shunt comes undone with the pulled minecart jettisoned backward. The correct way to make such a turn is having the shunt undone before a turn, and then make the two rejoin on a straight rail later by having the pulled cart catch up with the minecart with furnace.

text: Fuel is not stored as an item in the entity, but in the object data in the fuel property as a time in ticks. Fuel is a short value, i.e. a maximum of 32767 ticks, which is about 27 minutes. However, {{cmd|/summon furnace_minecart ~ ~ ~ {Fuel:32000} }} alone doesn't make it go since it doesn't have a direction. It can be right-clicked on a track to give it a direction, or it can be summoned with the properties PushX and PushZ set, which are responsible for the direction. The Motion property of every entity allows for movement of the minecart, but it does not direct the minecart to move on its own.

text: A minecart with hopper is a minecart with a hopper inside. Unlike a normal hopper, it pulls items from containers much more quickly, cannot push items into containers, can collect item entities through a single layer of solid blocks, and is locked and unlocked via activator rails.
search_text: Minecart with Hopper > Overview: A minecart with hopper is a minecart with a hopper inside. Unlike a normal hopper, it pulls items from containers much more quickly, cannot push items into containers, can collect item entities through a single layer of solid blocks, and is locked and unlocked via activator rails.

text: Similarly to other forms of minecart, minecarts with hoppers can be destroyed by attacking them, and doing so drops them as an item. Despite the appearance of the relevant particles, critical hits are not applied to them.
search_text: Minecart with Hopper > Crafting: Similarly to other forms of minecart, minecarts with hoppers can be destroyed by attacking them, and doing so drops them as an item. Despite the appearance of the relevant particles, critical hits are not applied to them.

text:
Minecarts with hoppers are placed similarly to other minecarts.
A minecart with hopper pulls in items lying nearby (within a range slightly larger than the cart itself), or inside a container directly above the minecart, at a high speed. In Java Edition a hopper minecart pulls items from a container with its bottom face 0.5 (exclusive) to 1.5 (inclusive) blocks directly above the bottom center of the minecart at a speed of one item every game tick in (20 items per second), eight times as fast as a normal hopper. In Bedrock Edition it pulls an item only every two game ticks (10 items per second), four times as fast as a normal hopper. It also picks up items that are lying on a block directly above the track. It does not push items into containers, but a hopper underneath the track can remove items from a minecart with hopper on the track. Ordinary hoppers can also drop items into a minecart with hopper like other containers, at the normal speed of 2.5 items per second. In Bedrock Edition a minecart with hopper on a curved rail pulls in items in a hopper lying in front of its moving direction and one block above if the hopper's output funnel is pointed downward and no block is below that hopper.
The minecart with hopper can be disabled by passing over a powered activator rail, and can be reenabled by an inactive activator rail.

text:
A dropper can insert items into a minecart with hopper if any part of the entity's hitbox is within the dropper's target block-space. A dropper can fill a minecart with hopper even if the latter has been locked by an activator rail.
An empty minecart with hopper can travel more than 85 blocks without stopping (as opposed to a normal cart going less than 12 blocks) from a dead stop using a two-powered track starter, even with another minecart in front of it. However, the distance traveled by a minecart with hopper depends on the hopper's load. Using a one-powered rail starter track, a minecart with an empty hopper travels 64 blocks until it stops (as opposed to an empty normal minecart going 8 blocks). The distance traveled diminishes non-linearly with increased hopper load; a minecart with a full hopper can travel only 16 blocks in this setup.

text: A minecart with TNT is a minecart with TNT inside of it. Unlike normal TNT, it can detonate instantly, and its blast radius and damage is increased by its speed at detonation.
search_text: Minecart with TNT > Overview: A minecart with TNT is a minecart with TNT inside of it. Unlike normal TNT, it can detonate instantly, and its blast radius and damage is increased by its speed at detonation.

text: Similarly to other forms of minecart, minecarts with TNT can be destroyed by attacking them, and doing so drops them as an item. Despite the appearance of the relevant particles, critical hits are not applied to them.
search_text: Minecart with TNT > Obtaining: Similarly to other forms of minecart, minecarts with TNT can be destroyed by attacking them, and doing so drops them as an item. Despite the appearance of the relevant particles, critical hits are not applied to them.

text:
A minecart with TNT detonates after a delay upon meeting these conditions:
It moves over a powered activator rail.
It is destroyed while in motion (except by a player in Creative mode).
It is destroyed by fire, lava, or an explosion.
It is hit by a fire charge projectile.
, by having a flint and steel, fire charge, or any item enchanted with Fire Aspect used on it.
The delay is for an activator rail, like the TNT block. For other causes, there is a random delay between 0 and 1.95 seconds.
It detonates instantly upon meeting these conditions:
It hits the ground with a downward velocity of having fallen more than three blocks, not landing on any form of rail.
It turns a corner on a track too fast, with a solid block or entity located in the direction of its initial momentum.
It is hit by a flaming projectile.
It collides with a block or entity at speed.
Upon detonation, it acts like normal TNT, exploding and damaging nearby blocks, players, and entities. Upon detonation by an activator rail, it does not destroy its rails and the blocks the rail is on, however other nearby minecarts can. More than one minecart can be placed on the same rail block, allowing many of them to fit in a single block space.

text:
The explosion has a base power of 4, the same as regular TNT, but the game also adds a random bonus value up to 1.5 times the minecart's velocity, but no higher than 7.5. This means that with a speed of 5 or higher the power is a random value between 4 and 11.5. When triggered by an activator rail or by damage, the bonus value is calculated using the horizontal velocity of the minecart. Due to a bug, the speed of a flaming arrow also influences the explosion power of stationary tnt minecarts. When triggered by fall damage, the fall distance divided by 10 is used.
Minecarts with TNT bounce off of other minecarts and cannot be linked to minecarts with furnaces.

text: Az aktív kén egy kénből készült blokk, amely hányingert okozó gázt bocsát ki, ha sekély víz alá helyezik. Ha egy magmablokkot helyeznek alá a sekély vízben, akkor gejzírré alakul, amely időnként kitör, és a magasba repíti a lényeket (entitásokat). Ha lávát helyeznek alá, az folyamatos, megállás nélküli kitörést okoz.

text:
Ha vízforrás alá helyezik, az aktív kén dekoratív fehér buborékoszlopot bocsát ki, amely a víz felszínén ártalmas gázzá alakul (amit sárga gázrészecskék jeleznek), ha bizonyos feltételek teljesülnek. Az ártalmas gáz kialakulásához az ktív kén feletti összes víztömbnek forrásblokknak kell lennie, az aktív kén legfeljebb 4 blokkal lehet a víz felszíne alatt, és a közvetlenül a felszín feletti blokknak levegőnek kell lennie. Az ártalmas gáz minden olyan felszíni vízforrás-blokkon kibocsátódik, amely felett levegő van, az aktív kén közvetlen feletti vízblokk központjától számított 3 blokkos sugarú körben.
Az ebben a vízben tartózkodó játékosok és mobok 4 másodperces Hányinger hatást kapnak környezeti effektusként, amely mindaddig megújul, amíg az entitás a vízen belül marad.

text:
Ha láva vagy magmablokk fölé, és egy 1-4 blokk magasságú vízforrás alá helyezik, az aktív kén gejzírré tör ki, amely az alatta lévő blokktól függően folyamatosan vagy időszakosan működik. Amikor az aktív kén blokk kitör, a gejzírt alkotó részecskék megjelennek a víz felszínén, és a benne lévő entitásokat (a víz alatt is) felfelé lökik.
A gejzír magassága a vízoszlop magasságától függ: 5 \times \text{magasság} (blokkban).

text:
Ha magmablokk fölé és egy 1-4 blokk magasságú vízforrás alá helyezik, a Aktív kén időnként kitörhet. Egy teljes ciklus 300 és 1200 játék-tick (15-60 másodperc) között zajlik le, míg maga a kitörési fázis 20 és 100 játék-tick (1-5 másodperc) között tart.
Amikor lehelyeznek egy aktív kén blokkot, a világban elfoglalt pozíciója alapján két véletlenszerű érték rendelődik hozzá: egy nyugalmi érték (15 és 30 között) és egy kitörési érték (1 és 2 között). A nyugalmi és a kitörési állapot közötti időközök a aktív kén feletti vízoszlop magasságától és ettől a két értéktől függnek:
nyugalmi fázis időtartama (másodpercben): 10 \times (\text{magasság} - 1) + \text{nyugalmi érték} ;
kitörési fázis időtartama (másodpercben): (\text{magasság} - 1) + \text{kitoresi érték} .
A gejzírek természetes módon generálódnak a felszínen a kénes források részeként, mivel azok magmablokkokat tartalmaznak. A kénbarlangokban található kéntavak nem tartalmaznak magmablokkokat az aktív kén alatt, így a gejzírek természetes módon nem találhatók meg a kénbarlangokban.

text: A buzogány (mace) egy közelharci fegyver, amellyel lecsapások (smash attacks) hajthatók végre. Ez a támadás annál nagyobb sebzést okoz, minél magasabbról esik le a játékos, mielőtt eltalálna egy lényt. A sikeres lecsapás megvédi a játékost, így nem szenvedi el a támadás előtt felhalmozott esési sebzést. Barkácsolásához egy nehéz mag (heavy core) szükséges, amely 7,5% eséllyel esik le a baljós ketrecekből (ominous vaults), valamint egy szélrúd, amelyet őrszelektől lehet szerezni.

text: A buzogány a földön állva is normál támadás végrehajtására, ami sebzést okoz, ha a támadási töltöttség teljesen feltöltődött. A Java Kiadásban, ez rendelkezik a játék leglassabb támadási sebességével (0,6). Normál használat esetén másodpercenként 3,6 sebzést (DPS) okoz, kritikus találatokkal pedig 5,4-et, míg egy fakard 6,4 DPS-t biztosít. Viszont a Java Kiadásban egy Páncéltörés (Breach) IV bűbájjal ellátott buzogány bír a harmadik legmagasabb DPS-sel és a legnagyobb ütéscsapásonkénti sebzéssel a gyémánt- vagy netherit páncélt viselő lények ellen. A Bedrock Kiadásban a támadási töltési idő hiánya miatt a Páncéltörés IV buzogányok nyújtják a legmagasabb ütéscsapásonkénti sebzést és a legnagyobb DPS-t a gyémánt- vagy netherit páncélosok ellen.

text: A buzogány akkor hajt végre lecsapást, ha a játékos legalább 1,5 blokknyi magasságból esik le a gomb megnyomásakor, függetlenül a buzogány aktuális újratöltöttségétől. A játékos nem állhat a földön és nem repülhet elytrával , az esési magasság kiszámítása pedig egyszerűen a kiindulási Y koordináta és a becsapódási Y koordináta különbsége. A sikeresen végrehajtott lecsapás anélkül, hogy a földet érnénk, visszaállítja az esési magasságot a lecsapás helyére, így teljesen semmissé teszi az esési sebzést. A játékos esési sebzése újra felhalmozódik, ha tovább zuhan.

text:
A lecsapás végrehajtásakor az eltalált lény plusz sebzést szenved el az esési magasság alapján. A támadás 2,5 blokkos körzetében lévő összes lény hátralökődik, a széllökés (wind charge) hatásához hasonlóan. A lecsapás bármilyen lényen vagy entitáson végrehajtható, beleértve a mobokat, játékosokat és az olyan tárgyakat is, mint a páncélállványok. A lecsapás nem hajtható végre, ha a játékoson aktív a Lassú esés (Slow Falling) effektus.
A kitinszárnnyal való ereszkedés blokkonkénti esésnek számít a lecsapások szempontjából. A Java Kiadásban a kitinszárnyt le kell venni a támadás előtt, mivel a kitinszárnyas repülés közben nem aktiválódik a lecsapás. A Bedrock Kiadásban nem szükséges levenni az elytrát, a lecsapás repülés közben is működésbe lép.
Ha a játékos sebzést szenved el a buzogánnyal való zuhanás közben, a lecsapáshoz számított magasság nem nullázódik le.

text: A Zombik, kiszáradt zombik, csontvázak, kóborlók (strays) és a láplövészek (bogged) kis eséllyel páncélt viselve jelenhetnek meg, ami csizmát is tartalmazhat. text: Minden egyes páncélpont 4%-kal csökkenti a kapott sebzést (additív módon növekedve). A páncélpontokat az életerősáv feletti páncélsávon megjelenő fél ingek jelzik. A páncélpontok hatékonysága csökken a beérkező támadások erejének növekedésével, ezt a hatást enyhíti a páncélkeménység (armor toughness). A páncélkeménységnek nincs vizuális jelzősávja. A csizma tartóssága minden beérkező sebzés után 1 ponttal csökken (lefelé kerekítve, de sosem 1 pont alá). A különböző csizmatípusok eltérő elbűvölhetőséggel rendelkeznek, ez az érték befolyásolja a közvetlenül a varázslóasztalból kapott bűbájok erejét. A netherit csizmák 1-es szintű (10%-os) hátralökési ellenállást biztosítanak.

text:
A fejszék egyedi képessége, hogy kritikus csapásokat (crushing blows) mérhetnek , amelyek 5 másodpercre letiltják a célpont pajzsának használatát. A zúzó csapások csak olyan célpontok ellen váltódnak ki, akik aktívan maguk előtt tartják a pajzsukat.
A zúzó csapások a célpont összes pajzsára hatással vannak, nem csak arra, amelyet éppen használt. A zúzó csapások nem váltódnak ki olyan célpontok ellen, akiknél a pajzs még nem lépte túl a 250 ms-os aktiválási késleltetést. A zúzó csapások a támadási újratöltési százaléktól függetlenül kiváltódnak, és a söprő támadásokkal (sweep attacks) ellentétben a kritikus találatokkal és a sprintelésből indított hátralökő támadásokkal egy időben is létrejöhetnek.
A zúzó csapások úgy működnek, hogy egy 5 másodperces használati újratöltési időt kényszerítenek ki. Amikor egy pajzs kábult, nem használható jobb klikkeléssel vagy osonással . A zúzó csapás végrehajtása nem fogyaszt tartósságot a fejszéből, hasonlóan ahhoz, ahogy a többi támadás sem fogyaszt tartósságot, ha egy pajzs blokkolja azt.
a játékos, akinek a pajzsa kábult, immunissá válik a hátralökésre néhány játéktikk erejéig.
A fejszét forgató mobok, mint például a puskások vagy a piglin dühöngők, szintén zúzó csapást mérnek, ha eltalálják a játékos pajzsát. A gondnok közelharci támadása szintén zúzó csapást hajt végre, ha a játékos pajzsával találkozik.

text:
Füves földblokkot úgy lehet beszerezni, ha egy Gyengéd Érintés bűbájjal ellátott eszközzel bányásszuk ki. Egyébként földet dob elpusztításakor.
A havas füves változat nem szerezhető be tárgyként a normál játékmeneten keresztül, még a Gyengéd Érintés használatával sem. A Java Kiadásban, a parancsok használhatók arra, hogy a játékosok olyan füves földblokkot kapjanak, amely lehelyezéskor havas állapotba kerül (pl. {{cmd|1=give minecraft:grass_block[minecraft:block_state={snowy:"true"}]}}).

A havas füves változat nem szerezhető be tárgyként a normál játékmeneten keresztül, még a Gyengéd Érintés használatával sem. text: A füves földblokkok természetes módon generálódnak számos biomban a Felszíni világban, valamint a falvak és az ősi városok részeként. A füves földblokkok korongok formájában generálódnak a sár között a mangrovemocsarakban.

text: Az endermanek fel tudják venni a füves földblokkokat, és ha megölik őket, eldobják a náluk lévő blokkot, így ez az egyetlen módja a füves földblokkok beszerzésének a Gyengéd Érintés használata nélkül.

text:
A fű átterjedhet a közeli föld blokkokra, de a terméketlen földre vagy a gyökeres földre nem. A fű játékos beavatkozása nélküli terjedése nagyban függ a nappali ciklustól. Ahhoz, hogy egy földblokk befogadja a füvet egy közeli füves földblokról, a következő követelményeknek kell teljesülniük:
A füvet fogadó földblokknak a forrás füves földblokk 3×5×3-as tartományán belül kell lennie, ahol a forrásblokk a tartomány második legfelső rétegének közepén helyezkedik el.
A forrás füves földblokk közvetlenül felette lévő sávban a fényszintnek legalább 9-esnek vagy világosabbnak kell lennie.
A földblokk közvetlenül felette lévő blokknak lehetővé kell tennie, hogy a fény áthaladjon rajta és elérje a földblokkot, bár a tényleges fényszint nem számít. Ez azt jelenti, hogy a fényt részben átengedő blokkoknak, mint például a lépcsőknek és a félblokkoknak, a fényblokkoló oldaluk nem nézhet a földblokk felé.
A földblokk közvetlenül felette lévő blokk nem lehet láva, víz vagy egy blokk vízzel elárasztott változata.

text:
A terméketlen föld megművelésével a játékos a sódert földdé alakíthatja. Két-két blokk sóderből és földből négy blokk terméketlen föld lesz, amelyet aztán le lehet helyezni és meg lehet művelni. Mivel a sóder megújítható a piglinekkel való cserekereskedelem révén, ez biztosítja a föld megújítható forrását.
Egy másik módszer a megújítható föld nyerésére a mohablokkok használata. Az azálea növekedés közben a közvetlenül alatta lévő mohablokkot gyökeres földdé alakítja, amikor azáleafává fejlődik. A Bedrock kiadásban a legtöbb facsemete közvetlenül a fa megnövekedése után (vagy akár egy perccel utána) a közvetlenül alatta lévő mohát földdé alakítja. A Java kiadásban a nagy lucfenyők növekedésük során akár 100 mohablokkot is podzollá alakítanak. Mivel a moha csontliszttel kőből is előállítható, a kő pedig vízzel és lávával végteleníthető, a föld mindaddig megújítható, amíg van hozzáférés vízhez, lávához és mohablokkokhoz.

text:
Egy foglalkozással rendelkező falusival vagy vándorkereskedőkkel való interakció megnyitja a kereskedési menüt, felfüggeszti az útvonalkeresésüket, és a kereskedő játékos felé fordítja őket. Ha a kereskedő megsebesül, vagy eltávolodik a játékostól, a kereskedési menü bezárul.
Minden tranzakció smaragddal történik. A kereskedés az egyetlen módja a gömb mintájú zászlóminta, a bomlás nyila , az összes falusi felfedező térkép, az óceáni templom térképe, a küzdőteres térkép és az erdei kastély térképe megszerzésének. Emellett ez az egyetlen megújuló módja a harangok, a gyémánt felszerelések (kivéve a gyémántpáncélt, a gyémántlándzsa, a gyémánt ló páncél és a gyémánt nautilusz páncél), a lapis lazuli , a varázslat palackjai, az üveg, a homok, a vörös homok, a korallblokkok és a kis csepplevelek megszerzésének.

text:
A falusiaknak öt karrierszintjük van, amelyeket kereskedéssel lehet növelni. Minden falusi a kezdő szinten indít. A falusi szintje látható a kereskedési menüben. A falusi által viselt kitűző mutatja a karrierszintjét: kő a kezdőnek, vas a tanoncnak, arany a mesterlegénynek, smaragd a szakértőnek és gyémánt a mesternek. A kereskedés mindaddig, amíg a falusi kereskedési sávja meg nem telik, feloldja a kereskedések következő szintjét. Amikor egy játékos kereskedik egy falusival, mind a falusi, mind a játékos tapasztalatot szerez. Minden falusi kereskedés 3–6 tapasztalattal jutalmazza a játékost, plusz további 5 tapasztalattal, ha a falusi szintet lép a kereskedéssel. A vándorkereskedőkkel való kereskedés szintén tapasztalattal jutalmazza a játékost, bár a kereskedőnek nincsenek megszerezhető tapasztalati szintjei. A falusi akkor lép szintet, amikor a tapasztalati sávja megtelik, és legfeljebb két vagy három új kereskedést nyer el, miközben megtartja a meglévő kereskedéseit.
Amikor egy falusi szintet lép a szakmájában, 10 másodperces Regeneráció I hatást kap (összesen gyógyulást), amely rózsaszín részecskéket bocsát ki. A falusi zöld, plusz alakú részecskéket is kibocsát.
A mester szintű kereskedések továbbra is tapasztalattal jutalmazzák a falusit, de ennek nincs tényleges hatása, mivel a falusi nem léphet tovább szintet.
Mindegyik kitűző 2×3 pixel méretű, kivéve a kezdő (kő) kitűzőt, amely 4×4 pixel.

text: A falusi szakmája határozza meg a kereskedései kiválasztásához használt kereskedési készletet. Például a szalmakalapot viselő falusiak földművesek, így kereskedéseik a Földműves kereskedési készleten alapulnak. Minden szakma az ajánlatok egy előre meghatározott és véges halmazát oldja fel. Ezenkívül egyetlen mennyiség sem mehet 1 alá vagy a stakk méreténél magasabbra.

A Java Kiadásban, az újratöltési idő egy olyan változatát használják, ahol a támadás nem lehetséges a 100%-os töltöttség eléréséig, ellentétben a többi fegyverrel.
A Bedrock Kiadásban, ehelyett egy olyan használati újratöltési idővel rendelkeznek, mint az Endertojás (Ender pearl), ami hasonló kényszerített hatást vált ki. Ez a használati cooldown az eszköztárban lévő összes lándzsaszintre élesedik, nem csak arra, amellyel a döfést végezték.
A lándzsával továbbra is végrehajtható rohamtámadás, miközben a döfés éppen újratöltődik, így a döfések és rohamok váltogatásával a támadási ráta gyakorlatilag megduplázható. A döfések eggyel több sebzést okoznak -ben, mint -ben. A lándzsára való átváltás -ben nem igényel azonnali töltési időt, ellentétben a verzióval. Bedrock Edition-ben a döfés után van néhány ticknyi késleltetés, ami alatt a rohamtámadás nem indítható el.

text:
A lándzsa alternatívaként támadási pozícióba engedhető a gomb nyomva tartásával; ekkor a célponttal való ütközés a felhasználó és a célpont sebességétől függő sebzést okoz. A rohamtámadásokhoz másodpercenként 5,1 blokknyi mozgási sebességkülönbség szükséges a támadó és a célpont között a sebzés kiosztásához. Emiatt a hátrafelé hátráló mobok, mint a csontvázak, gyakran csak lökést (knockback) szenvednek el a rohamokktól. A rohamtámadások több lényt is eltalálhatnak, és -ben 0,5 másodperces (10 tick) késleltetés van a rohamtalálatok becsapódásai között. A rohamtámadás akkor is bevihető, ha a döfés éppen újratöltődik. A rohamtámadások három fázison mennek keresztül kitartott helyzetben:
Készenléti (Engaged)
A rohamtámadás első fázisa, amelyet a stabilan előretartott lándzsa jelez.
A támadás sebez, lökést okoz, és leveti a megtámadott célpontokat a hátasaikról.
Fáradó (Tired)
A rohamtámadás második fázisa, amelyet a lándzsa oldalra fordulása és remegése jelez.
A támadás sebez és lökést okoz.
Leengedett (Disengaged)
A rohamtámadás utolsó fázisa, amelyet a képernyő aljára süllyedő lándzsa jelez.
A támadás már csak tisztán sebez.

A mellvért tartóssága minden beérkező sebzés után 1 ponttal csökken (lefelé kerekítve, de sosem 1 pont alá). A különböző mellvérttípusok eltérő elbűvölhetőséggel rendelkeznek, ez az érték befolyásolja a közvetlenül a varázslóasztalból kapott bűbájok erejét. A netherit mellvértek 1-es szintű (10%-os) hátralökési ellenállást biztosítanak.

text: A sisak (helmet) (a bőrből készült változatot sapka néven, a teknőspáncélból készültet pedig teknőspáncél néven ismerik) egy fejre vehető páncéldarab. A sisakoknak hét elsődleges szintje van: bőr, arany, réz, vas, láncpáncél, gyémánt és netherit. A teknőspáncél egy másik fajta sisak, amely Vízalatti légzés (Water Breathing) effektust biztosít viselőjének, valamint felhasználható a Teknősmester főzeteinek főzéséhez is.

A Zombik, kiszáradt zombik, csontvázak, kóborlók, láplövészek és a piglinek kis eséllyel páncélt viselve jelenhetnek meg. Halálukkor 8,5% esély van arra (9,5% Zsákmányolás I, 10,5% Zsákmányolás II és 11,5% Zsákmányolás III bűbájjal), hogy leejtik a fejükön lévő sisakot, kivéve, ha egy baljós próbaidézőből (ominous trial spawner) teremtek meg. A leejtett sisak általában erősen sérült, és 5-19-es szintű bűbájokkal lehet elbűvölve.
A Bedrock Kiadásban, a portyázások során megidéződő Bosszúállók (vindicators) és Rablók (pillagers) 4,16% eséllyel (nehéz nehézségi szinten 5,128% eséllyel) ejtenek le egy vas sisakot. A leejtett sisak általában erősen sérült, és 50% eséllyel van ellátva egy véletlenszerű bűbájjal.

A tárgy (item) egy olyan objektum, amely létezhet a játékosok, mobok vagy páncélállványok eszköztárában (inventory); különféle tárolóblokkokban (például ládákban vagy adagolókban), valamint eszközkeretekben, világító eszközkeretekben és polcokon.

text:
Némelyik tárgy, amikor (used), elhelyezi a saját blokk- (ItemBlock) vagy lény- (csille, idéző tojások stb.) változatát a világban. Egyszerűen megfogalmazva: az eszköztárban tárgynak számítanak, lehelyezve pedig blokknak. Például a csónakok lehelyezve lénnyé (entity) válnak, az ágyak pedig blokkok egy csoportjává alakulnak. Amikor kiválasztják őket a gyorselérési sávban (hotbar), a tárgyak rövid időre megjelenítik a nevüket a HUD felett.
Az egyetlen módszer, amellyel egy tárgy megfelelően megjeleníthető a játékkörnyezetben, ha elhelyezzük egy eszközkeretben, polcon vagy egy páncélállványon. A megjelenített tárgyak – akár ezeken a blokkokon, akár kézben (külső és belső nézetben egyaránt), akár eldobva – a játékban MERS textúrakészletekkel renderelődnek az élénk látvány (Vibrant Visuals) segítségével, és árnyékokat, tükröződéseket vagy kausztikus fényhatásokat mutathatnak. Számos tárgy kibocsátó világítással (emissive lighting) rendelkezik, és világít a sötétben.

text:
Ha egy olyan tárgyat dobnak el, amelyből lehelyezve nem lesz blokk, akkor egy lebegő sprite-ként ábrázolt lénnyé (entity) válik a föld felett. 5 percig marad meg egy betöltött chunkban, mielőtt eltűnne (despawn) – kivéve a Nethercsillagot –, hacsak a játékos át nem megy rajta, hogy felvegye, fel nem veszi egy mob, egy tölcsér vagy egy tölcséres csille, vagy meg nem semmisíti tűz, láva, kaktusz, robbanás, vákuum (void) vagy a parancs.
Az eldobott netherit tárgyakat a tűz vagy a láva nem tudja megsemmisíteni, az eldobott Netheritcsillagokat pedig a robbanások nem pusztítják el.
A víz alá került tárgyak felemelkednek a víz felszíne felé. Ha a víz áramlik, az objektumot sodorja magával az ár.
A tölcsérek minden felettük elhelyezkedő tárgyat beszívnak, feltéve, hogy nincsenek redstone-jellel aktiválva.

A tárgyak vagy 64-es, vagy 16-os méretig halmozhatók (stackelhetők), vagy egyáltalán nem halmozhatók:
A legtöbb tárgy 64-ig halmozható. Ide tartozik az összes teljes blokk, amelyek körvonalai lehelyezéskor egy egész blokknyi helyet foglalnak el.
Néhány tárgy, például a hógolyók, az üres vödrök, a tojások, a táblák és az Endergyöngyok legfeljebb 16-os halmokba rendezhetők.
Bizonyos tárgyak egyáltalán nem halmozhatók, mint például a tartóssággal rendelkező elemek (fegyverek, páncélok és eszközök), a megtöltött vödrök és a bájitalok.
Technikai szempontból minden tárgy kényszeríthető arra, hogy parancsok segítségével egészen 99-ig vagy 127-ig halmozódjon.

text:
Az eszköztárban lévő 3D-s tárgyak (vagyis a blokkokéi) gyakran ezen modellekként jelennek meg a lapos grafikák helyett. Ezeknek a tárgyaknak a megjelenését befolyásolja az árnyékolás, amely a játékverziók során alapértelmezetten megváltozott, és a modellen belül a „gui_light” paraméterrel módosítható. A 3D-s tárgyak alapértelmezett értéke az „side” (oldal), míg a lapos tárgyaké a „front” (elölnézet).
A következő táblázatok egy tiszta fehér textúra használatának eredményeit mutatják be, feltételezve a 854x480-as alapértelmezett ablakos felbontást.
Eszköztárban lévő tárgyak (Inventory items)
A Beta 1.8 Pre-release-től a 12w32a-ig az eszköztárban lévő tárgyak sötétebben renderelődtek, mint a gyorselérési sávban vagy a ládákban. Nem ismert, miért volt ez így. Mind a 3D-s, mind a lapos tárgyak érintettek voltak. Ezt végül a 12w34a verzióban javították.
Elforgatott blokktárgyak
A 1.8 snapshotjaiban (14w10a-tól 14w21b-ig) bizonyos, általában elérhetetlen sérülési értékekkel rendelkező tárgyak (kifejezetten az elforgatott rönkök, szénabálák és kvarcoszlopok) blokklaponkénti árnyékintenzitása más módon változott, mint a többi blokktárgyé. Az árnyékolás szintje továbbra is megegyezik az ezen verziótartományban lévő tipikus blokkokéval, egyszerűen egy 90 fokos elforgatással a 3D-ben, ami vagy egy 120 fokos tükröződésként, vagy egy vízszintes tükrözéssel ellátott formában jelent meg a 2D-ben.
Korai Indev világbetöltés

Í Minecraft er kubbum raðað upp í þrívítt net (e.g. teningslaga hreiður) af 1 rúmmetra sellum, þó svo að sumir kubbar virðist aðeins taka upp hluta úr sellu. text:
Sumir kubbar, eins og (sea lantern) og glowstone, emit light, the amount of which varies widely; see this table of light values for further information. Opaque blocks completely block light, while transparent blocks have no effect on light, block the light, or merely weaken it.
Almost all blocks ignore gravity, except for sand, red sand, gravel, anvils of all damage levels, dragon eggs, all colors of concrete powder, scaffolding, snow layers , pointed dripstone, suspicious sand, and suspicious gravel. These turn into entities when their support is removed.
When broken, blocks emit sounds and particles associated with themselves, except in the following cases:
If the block is affected by gravity and falls into an invalid space, such as sand falling onto a torch.
Anvils that are destroyed by running out of durability or falling. A different sound is played, but there are no particles.
If the block is washed away by a fluid.
If the block is replaced by another block.
If the block's supporting block is removed.
If the block is leaves and decays.

Opaque blocks completely block light, while transparent blocks have no effect on light, block the light, or merely weaken it.
Almost all blocks ignore gravity, except for sand, red sand, gravel, anvils of all damage levels, dragon eggs, all colors of concrete powder, scaffolding, snow layers , pointed dripstone, suspicious sand, and suspicious gravel. These turn into entities when their support is removed.
When broken, blocks emit sounds and particles associated with themselves, except in the following cases:
If the block is affected by gravity and falls into an invalid space, such as sand falling onto a torch.
Anvils that are destroyed by running out of durability or falling. A different sound is played, but there are no particles.
If the block is washed away by a fluid.
If the block is replaced by another block.
If the block's supporting block is removed.
If the block is leaves and decays.

text:
Most block textures are 16×16 pixels and control color/transparency. The size of a block defaults to 1 cubic meter but can be resized via models; some, like logs, have different textures per face.
Animated textures appear on: water, lava, fire, Nether portals, prismarine, and many more. A few blocks use special rendering, such as the starfield effect for End portals and End gateways.
With Vibrant Visuals and ray tracing, extra maps are used: MERS (MER with ray tracing) defines metallic (reflects light), emissive (glows), and rough (absorbs light) per pixel; subsurface scattering applies to Vibrant Visuals. Normal and heightmaps add 3D depth.
Resource packs can change resolution, animation, shapes/models, and scale blocks to any equal width/height — 2^n (e.g., 16×16, 8×8) work best.

text:
Piesok sa prirodzene generuje v mnohých biómoch Overworldu, v diskovitých formáciách v blízkosti rybníkov a riek. Generuje sa v hojnom množstve v púštiach a na plážach, zvyčajne v štvorblokových vrstvách, podopretých pieskovcom. Piesok sa tiež generuje ako oceánske dno vlažných oceánov, hlbokých vlažných oceánov a teplých oceánov v jednej vrstve, ktorú nepodopiera sandstone. V nepúštnych biómoch sa zvyčajne generuje v priemere 545 blokov na chunk.
Piesok sa tiež používa na zakrytie zakopaných truhlíc, v závislosti od toho, kde sa truhlica vygeneruje. (V tomto prípade sa piesok používa na zakrytie zakopaných truhlíc, ktoré sa vytvárajú na plážach a oceánskych dnách zložených z piesku, ale v niektorých prípadoch sa namiesto piesku môže použiť kameň alebo pieskovec).
Piesok sa tiež generuje ako súčasť ruín v teplých oceánoch a niektorých ruín v studených oceánoch, niektorých domov v púštnych dedinách, púštnych studniach, púštnych pyramídach a má šancu generovať sa vo vchodoch do skúšobných komôr.

text:
Ak sa odstráni blok pod blokom piesku, piesok začne padať, kým nedopadne na ďalší dostupný blok.
Ak padajúci piesok pristane a zakryje hlavu moba alebo hráča, mob alebo hráč v ňom zahrabaný neustále dostáva udusenie. Ak padajúci piesok dopadne do priestoru, ktorý zaberá nepevný blok (ako napríklad pochodeň, koľajnica alebo redstone prach) alebo blok menší ako celý blok (ako napríklad pôlblok alebo dušný piesok), piesok spadne a zmení sa na predmet. Ak spadne na pavučinu, padá pomaly, kým ňou úplne neprejde.
Hoci TNT nerozbije žiadne bloky, ak exploduje pod vodou, ak piesok spadne a zakryje TNT pred jeho explóziou, bloky sa rozbijú ako obvykle.

Khi được đặt lên trên hay phía dưới một khối, cần gạt sẽ hướng thẳng hàng với hướng của người chơi.
, cần gạt có thể đặt được lên cả hàng rào, tường và phễu, thậm chí đặt được dưới nước.
Khi được đặt lên mặt bên của một khối, phía dưới là bật và phía trên là tắt. Trên mặt trên hoặc mặt dưới của một khối, tắt là bắc hoặc tây, bật là nam hoặc đông.

text:
Cột băng là một khối có đầu nhọn, thường xuất hiện trong các hang động băng. Chúng có thể tự nhiên hình thành và phát triển trên trần hang dưới dạng nhũ đá băng, nhưng cũng có thể được người chơi đặt thủ công trên mặt đất dưới dạng măng đá băng. Khi tiếp xúc với đủ lượng ánh sáng từ môi trường xung quanh, các cột băng có thể tan chảy và vỡ ra.
Các nhũ đá băng treo ở mặt dưới của các khối và phát triển theo thời gian khi đáp ứng một số điều kiện nhất định. Khi khối nâng đỡ chúng bị phá hủy, nhũ đá băng sẽ rơi xuống và gây sát thương cho các thực thể mà chúng va chạm.
Các măng đá băng nằm trên mặt trên của các khối. Chúng làm tăng sát thương do rơi đối với người chơi và thực thể khi tiếp đất lên chúng.

text: Cột băng có thể được khai thác bằng bất kỳ công cụ nào, nhưng cuốc chim là nhanh nhất. Cột băng sẽ vỡ ngay lập tức khi bị đánh trúng bởi đinh ba; tuy nhiên chúng không thể bị phá bởi bất kì vật bắn nào khác. Các măng đá băng cũng bị phá khi chúng tan chảy.

text:
Một cột băng chỉ có thể phát triển khi được treo trực tiếp bên dưới một khối băng nén. Cột băng phát triển theo chiều hướng xuống dưới, tạo thành nhũ băng với chiều dài tối đa là 5 khối. Tuy nhiên, người chơi có thể tăng chiều dài của nó bằng cách đặt thêm các cột băng thủ công. Không giống như thạch nhũ nhọn và gai lưu huỳnh, cột băng không thể phát triển thành măng đá. Cột băng không thể phát triển nếu đầu nhọn của chúng ngập nước. Cột băng cũng không thể phát triển ở nơi khiến nó bị tan chảy.
Cột băng phát triển khá chậm, với thời gian trung bình khoảng 5 ngày trong trò chơi (100 phút) cho mỗi lần phát triển thêm một khối. Cụ thể hơn, mỗi khi đầu nhọn của cột băng nhận được một lượt cập nhật ngẫu nhiên, sẽ có một xác suất nhỏ là 1,138% ( ) để cột băng phát triển thêm một khối.

text:
Khi nhận được một lượt cập nhật ngẫu nhiên, cột băng sẽ tan chảy nếu đáp ứng một trong các điều kiện sau. Phần gốc của cột băng (tức đoạn được gắn vào một bề mặt kín hoàn toàn) không bao giờ tan chảy.
Cấp độ ánh sáng khối tại vị trí của nó từ 5 trở lên.
Khối nằm bên dưới nó từ 1 đến 2 ô là một khối magma.
Cột băng được đặt trong Nether, bất kể cấp độ ánh sáng.
Khi tan chảy, nhũ đá băng cùng tất cả các đoạn cột băng nối bên dưới sẽ rơi xuống dưới dạng khối rơi, trong khi măng đá băng cùng tất cả các đoạn cột băng nối bên trên sẽ bị phá vỡ và rơi ra dưới dạng vật phẩm..

text:
Nhũ đá băng được tạo ra khi đặt cột băng bên dưới một khối có mặt đáy kín hoàn toàn.
Nếu khối nâng đỡ nhũ đá băng hoặc bất kỳ khối nào thuộc nhũ đá băng bị phá vỡ hoặc tan chảy, thì tất cả các đoạn cột băng không còn được nâng đỡ sẽ rơi xuống, gây sát thương cho người chơi và sinh vật đứng bên dưới, tương tự như một chiếc đe hoặc thạch nhũ nhọn rơi xuống. Khi người chơi chết do bị nhũ đá băng rơi trúng, thông báo chết " đã bị đâm bởi thạch nhũ rơi xuống" sẽ xuất hiện.

Nếu khối nâng đỡ nhũ đá băng hoặc bất kỳ khối nào thuộc nhũ đá băng bị phá vỡ hoặc tan chảy, thì tất cả các đoạn cột băng không còn được nâng đỡ sẽ rơi xuống, gây sát thương cho người chơi và sinh vật đứng bên dưới, tương tự như một chiếc đe hoặc thạch nhũ nhọn rơi xuống. text:
Măng đá băng được tạo ra khi đặt cột băng lên trên một khối có mặt trên kín hoàn toàn. Chúng không xuất hiện tự nhiên trong thế giới.
Khi rơi trúng khối trên cùng của măng đá băng, khoảng cách rơi sẽ được nhân đôi để tính tổng sát thương do rơi, sử dụng công thức ceil(fall_distance × 2 − 2) . Người chơi hoặc sinh vật sẽ chịu sát thương mỗi khi nhảy lên trên một khối măng đá băng đơn lẻ (với độ cao nhảy thông thường là khối). Quãng đường di chuyển trong lượt cập nhật trò chơi cuối cùng khi rơi không được tính vào phép tính này, khiến kết quả có sai lệch đôi chút ở những khoảng cách rơi lớn hơn; xem thêm .
Nếu người chơi chết do rơi trúng măng đá băng, thông báo chết " đã bị đâm bởi một măng đá" sẽ xuất hiện.
Tất cả sinh vật miễn nhiễm với sát thương do rơi đều không chịu sát thương khi rơi xuống măng đá băng; Điều tương tự cũng áp dụng với người chơi nếu luật chơi được đặt thành false .
Người chơi có thể leo lên những đoạn măng đá băng được cấu thành hoàn toàn từ các phần có kích thước khác nhau, nhờ sự khác biệt về kích thước hộp va chạm của các cột băng tạo nên chúng.

text:
Mobs spawn in various ways. Most mobs spawn naturally, depending on the light level, biome, and their surroundings. For example, most animals are found in bright areas on the surface, while hostile monsters are commonly found in the dark (whether it's a cave, monster room, mansion, or at night). Animals usually spawn upon chunk generation, while hostile monsters spawn and despawn in a certain radius around the player.
Some mobs, including passive and neutral animals, and even hoglins, have the ability to be bred by the player, creating offspring. Villagers cannot be directly bred by the player, instead randomly breeding depending on the time of day, food (carrots, potatoes, and other crops), and the number of beds, which allows players to manipulate their likelihood of breeding.
Most mobs never spawn on transparent blocks, in water (except aquatic creatures), in lava (except for striders), on bedrock, or on blocks less than a full block tall (such as slabs placed on the bottom half). The exception is monster spawners, from which monsters can spawn naturally on any block including air.
Some mobs (like the snow golem and the wither) require that the player "construct" them before being able to spawn. The iron golem can spawn naturally and can also be constructed. The ender dragon can be respawned with four end crystals. A rare occurrence of spawning are the jockey mobs, which is a mob riding another mob.

text: Mobs are affected by the environment in the same ways as the player; they are subject to physics, and they can be hurt by the same things that harm the player (catching on fire, falling, drowning, attacks from weapons, the /kill command, etc.). Some mobs may be resistant or immune to certain hazards, such as some Nether mobs, which are immune to fire. All aquatic mobs except dolphins are immune to drowning. Mobs can ride minecarts and other mobs can climb up ladders. When mobs are killed, they turn to smoke particles and drop items that may be useful resources.

text:
Each type of mob in Minecraft has a certain AI (artificial intelligence) system with different behaviors and mechanics. Mobs ordinarily wander around at random if there is a player within 32 blocks and usually avoid walking off blocks high enough to cause falling damage. Many mobs have an advanced path-finding system that allows them to navigate through obstacles to get to a desired object or destination. Passive mobs flee in random directions after being hurt, while hostile mobs face and chase/attack the player as soon as the player comes close. Neutral mobs remain neutral until a player or mob provokes it (usually by attacking), at which point the neutral mob becomes hostile toward and attacks the entity that hit it. Most mobs are aware of players within (a Euclidian distance) 16 blocks of them, but some can see farther. Conversely, most mobs can be heard by players up to 16 blocks away. Mobs are harmless to players in Creative mode.
Most mobs cannot see through most solid blocks, including semi-transparent blocks such as ice, glass, tall grass, or glass panes. , all mobs (except for wardens ) try to avoid walking over rails unless pushed onto the rails by other mobs.
Using specific name tags on mobs can result in unusual behavior or rendering. See for details.

text:
Giống như những loại lanterns khác, đèn lồng cũng có thể đặt lên trên, hoặc treo dưới bề mặt của hầu hết các khối solid (một số khối yêu cầu ).
Để đặt đèn lồng lên trên một khối, hãy hướng lên mặt trên của khối đó, và nhấn . Để treo đèn lồng bên duới một khối, hãy hướng vào mặt dưới của khối đó, và nhấn . Cũng giống như những đèn lồng khác, nếu đèn lồng treo bên dưới một dây xích, đèn lồng và dây xích sẽ kết nối liền mạch với nhau.
Đèn lồng cũng có thể được đặt bằng cách nhấn lên một khối kế bên một khối không khí, giống như những loại đèn lồng khác. Nhấn lên nửa trên của khối kế bên sẽ treo đèn lồng bên dưới khối phía trên nó, và nhấn lên nửa dưới của khối kế bên sẽ đặt đèn lồng lên mặt trên của khối phía dưới nó.
Giống như những loại đèn lồng khác, nếu đèn lồng tồn tại ở một bề mặt không hợp lệ (một bề mặt mà bình thường đèn lồng không thể đặt lên), đèn lồng sẽ bị phá và rơi ra, bề mặt không hợp lệ được nhận từ một cập nhật khối.

text: A mob (short for mobile entity, or mobile object) is a game entity controlled by its own mob AI. All mobs can be attacked or hurt (from falling, attacked by a player or another mob, falling into the void, hit by an arrow, etc. with the exception of natural creakings), and have some form of voluntary movement. Different types of mobs often have unique AI and loot.
